## Proof

**Setup.** We are given an arithmetic function $f$ with mean value $M(f) = A \neq 0$, i.e.,
$$S(x) := \sum_{n \leq x} f(n) = Ax + E(x), \qquad E(x) = o(x) \quad (x \to \infty).$$
We seek an asymptotic formula for $T(x) := \sum_{n \leq x} f(n)\, n^{i\alpha}$, where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ is fixed.

**Tool: Abel (partial) summation.** For any arithmetic function $a(n)$ with partial sums $A(t) = \sum_{n \le t} a(n)$ and any $C^1$ function $g$ on $[1,\infty)$:
$$\sum_{n \le x} a(n)\, g(n) = A(x)\,g(x) - \int_1^x A(t)\, g'(t)\, dt.$$
We apply this with $a = f$ and $g(t) = t^{i\alpha}$, so $g'(t) = i\alpha\, t^{i\alpha - 1}$:
$$T(x) = S(x)\, x^{i\alpha} - i\alpha \int_1^x S(t)\, t^{i\alpha - 1}\, dt.$$

**Substitute $S(t) = At + E(t)$.** This gives
$$T(x) = \bigl(Ax + E(x)\bigr)\, x^{i\alpha} - i\alpha \int_1^x \bigl(At + E(t)\bigr)\, t^{i\alpha - 1}\, dt.$$

Split into main and error parts:
$$T(x) = \underbrace{A\, x^{1+i\alpha} - i\alpha\, A \int_1^x t^{i\alpha}\, dt}_{\text{main}} \;+\; \underbrace{E(x)\, x^{i\alpha} - i\alpha \int_1^x E(t)\, t^{i\alpha - 1}\, dt}_{\text{error}}.$$

**Evaluate the main term.** Since $i\alpha \neq -1$ (as $\alpha$ is real, $1 + i\alpha \neq 0$):
$$\int_1^x t^{i\alpha}\, dt = \frac{t^{1+i\alpha}}{1+i\alpha}\Bigg|_1^x = \frac{x^{1+i\alpha} - 1}{1+i\alpha}.$$
Therefore
$$A\, x^{1+i\alpha} - i\alpha\, A \cdot \frac{x^{1+i\alpha}-1}{1+i\alpha} = A\, x^{1+i\alpha}\!\left(1 - \frac{i\alpha}{1+i\alpha}\right) + \frac{i\alpha\, A}{1+i\alpha} = \frac{A\, x^{1+i\alpha}}{1+i\alpha} + \frac{i\alpha\, A}{1+i\alpha}.$$
The constant $\frac{i\alpha A}{1+i\alpha}$ is $O(1) = o(x)$.

**Bound the error terms.** Since $|x^{i\alpha}| = 1$ and $E(x) = o(x)$:
$$\bigl|E(x)\, x^{i\alpha}\bigr| = |E(x)| = o(x).$$

For the integral, note $|t^{i\alpha - 1}| = t^{-1}$. Given $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists $t_0$ such that $|E(t)| < \varepsilon\, t$ for all $t \ge t_0$. Then
$$\left|\int_{t_0}^x E(t)\, t^{i\alpha-1}\, dt\right| \le \int_{t_0}^x |E(t)|\, t^{-1}\, dt < \varepsilon \int_{t_0}^x dt = \varepsilon\,(x - t_0) = O(\varepsilon\, x).$$
The portion $\int_1^{t_0}$ is $O(1)$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, $\int_1^x E(t)\, t^{i\alpha-1}\, dt = o(x)$, and multiplying by the fixed constant $i\alpha$ preserves this.

**Combine.** All error terms are $o(x)$, so
$$T(x) = \frac{A\, x^{1+i\alpha}}{1+i\alpha} + o(x).$$

Since $A \neq 0$, the main term has magnitude $\frac{|A|\, x}{\sqrt{1+\alpha^2}} = \Theta(x)$, so $o(x)$ is genuinely lower order. We conclude:

$$\boxed{\sum_{n \le x} f(n)\, n^{i\alpha} \;=\; \frac{A}{1+i\alpha}\, x^{1+i\alpha} \;+\; o(x) \qquad (x \to \infty).}$$

Equivalently, $\sum_{n \le x} f(n)\, n^{i\alpha} \sim \dfrac{A}{1+i\alpha}\, x^{1+i\alpha}$.
